analysis:
This batch contains only CHANGELOG.md. The change replaces the v0.10.0 candidate header (base lines 11-13) with v0.10.1 candidate notes (head lines 11-138). Base lines 2243-2739 are unchanged historical entries. Changelog prose is documentation, not a control, so no finding cites it.

The notes describe these code changes, none of which are visible here:
- Verified-weight hash reuse (head 45-46). A coordinator-mode start reuses GLM's last verified hash when each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. The record is ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json, owner-only. This touches T-012, T-027, A-004 and TB-003: the operator owns the file, and an operator may preserve inode metadata while altering content. The notes say the managed load still SHA-256-verifies every file against the manifest before serving, and a file identity change during the load fails it. Verify that in source.
- Page-cache cache drop after hashing (head 72-74). Check for availability or admission (T-016) and memory-accounting effects.
- New desktop control API (head 89-95, 121-122). It is an authenticated loopback service run as LaunchAgent io.darkbloom.desktop-api, with a desktop_account device-code purpose and hardware telemetry. This is new local attack surface under TB-003/A-008. Review loopback auth, token scope, and that it cannot change provider credentials or serving. Also review the stale-process kill based on a recorded pid plus exact command.
- Withheld-until-validated JSON and forced-tool output (head 35-36). This is TB-007 and A-001 output handling.
- Nemotron Super media body bound raised from 8 to 40 MiB (head 57-59). This is a memory DoS concern.
- Console link page sending the purpose with the approval (head 126). This is platform-owned.

No security regression is established from changelog text alone. The integration pass must examine the corresponding provider source, especially the verified-weights record and the desktop API auth.
